analysis: Examined CI test-script changes only: scripts/test-cluster-test-plan.py (head 301-307) now asserts the non-blocking test-cluster-gpu job reads a per-shard Darkbloom route lane (fromJSON(inputs.routes)[format('test-cluster-gpu-{0}', matrix.shard)]) instead of a literal Blacksmith runner. scripts/test-darkbloom-route.py (head ~47-157, 234-236, 612-953) adds a DISPATCH-counted desktop-package macOS lane in desktop.yml, routes test-cluster-gpu-1..3 lanes, marks build-cluster/build-provider/cluster-release-checks as not `required` (so they request Darkbloom sandboxes even when sizes are off), removes UNROUTED_MACOS, and changes some lane sizes. These are test pins of CI routing; they do not touch provider runtime, attestation, encryption, cache (T-041), add-on hold (TB-012), or release signing paths. The UNROUTED list of credentialed/release workflows (base 139-141) is unchanged, so release-swift/release-provider/release-desktop still keep literal runners per the tests. Residual integration questions (outside supplied evidence): the actual workflow YAMLs (provider-tests.yml, provider-plan.yml, desktop.yml) are not supplied; reviewers should confirm desktop-package on workflow_dispatch running on routed self-hosted runners has no signing/notarization secrets (release-desktop.yml stays unrouted), and that build-provider/cluster-release-checks moving onto self-hosted sandboxes does not feed artifacts into release builds (A-011/A-017 provenance). The tests pin read-only permissions and fork-PR exclusion (base 516-528). No threat-model regression identified from the supplied test code itself.
